messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - canary-release error-rate spike on service=inference-api, route=/v1/stream (triggered by rollout v2026-03-14_21)
incident-bot: Alert details: 5m error-rate > 6% (baseline 0.4%), p95 latency +600ms, autosuppress=off
incident-bot: Fired to oncall: @oncall-mira (rotation: infra-sre)

oncall-mira: ack
oncall-mira: I'm up. seeing the PD notification. grabbing logs now — sam, are you on the release?

sam-eng: yep i'm here, pushed the canary earlier at 21:05 UTC. CI/rollback gate looked green. watching metrics.

charlie-sre: joining. initial glance: 503s from embed proxy, errors seem to correlate with hosts in pool `canary-east-2a-gpu-3`.

oncall-mira: good call. ops-bot: can you dump recent deploy annotation and canary instance set?

ops-bot: Top: deploy v2026-03-14_21, canary ring: 2/12 nodes (east-2a-gpu-3 x2). Canary config: traffic=10% -> 25% ramp.

sam-eng: we did the 10% ramp. looks like healthchecks passed at 10% then we auto-ramped to 25% around 21:12.

charlie-sre: logs (tail) show repeated kernel-level OOMs on one canary host:
```
[2026-03-14T21:13:05Z] runtime: GPU OOM - alloc 12.3GB failed
[2026-03-14T21:13:06Z] inference-runtime: stream loop crashed (sigsegv) -> 503
```

oncall-mira: ok that maps to p95 spike. tentative impact: canary nodes are unhealthy and returning 5xx, traffic balancer still routing some requests -> global error-rate bump.

pm-liz: any customer-facing impact? Support dashboard shows a handful of erroring requests for customers on the staging / early adopter list. Not widespread yet but could escalate.

support-jordan: just got two tickets flagged by automated monitor (beta clients). I'll open a banner draft but won't send until we confirm rollback.

sam-eng: plan: isolate canary nodes from LB (drain), scale up healthy pool, and roll back the canary artifact. options:
- quick rollback to previous image (v2026-03-13_18)
- isolate by removing 2 problematic hosts and let autoscale replace

charlie-sre: recommend immediate drain + rollback. draining first to stop new errors, rollback to known-good, then monitor.

oncall-mira: do it. sam, can you trigger rollback? charlie, can you coordinate drain and k8s node cordon?

sam-eng: initiating rollback now. command:
```
redwood deploy rollback --service inference-api --to v2026-03-13_18 --strategy immediate
```

sam-eng: rollback command returned: started rollback job id=rb-7832. ETA ~90s per pod termination/replace.

charlie-sre: cordoning nodes `canary-east-2a-gpu-3-1` and `...-2` and draining pods. logs:
```
kubectl cordon canary-east-2a-gpu-3-1
kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets canary-east-2a-gpu-3-1
```

ops-bot: LB config updated: removed 2 endpoints from canary target group. Traffic now at ~8% to canary pool (should drop to 0 as rollback finishes).

oncall-mira: monitoring metrics dashboard -> error-rate trending down from 6% to 1.8% over last 2 mins. p95 latency dropping. good sign.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Update - alert suppressed (auto) due to mitigation actions in-flight. Will remain open until rollout/rollback completes or SLO stable.

sam-eng: rollback is progressing; new pods coming up on v2026-03-13_18. seeing successful readiness probes.

charlie-sre: double-check: node crash reason appears to be a memory leak triggered by a new attention kernel path in the canary build. we captured a core dump and stacktrace.

oncall-mira: @pm-liz please pause the rest of the staged rollout and revoke further auto-ramps. set rollout to manual.

pm-liz: pausing now. I've toggled the rollout: auto-ramp disabled; notify release owners to hold. :white_flag:

support-jordan: pre-baked status banner ready: "We detected elevated errors for a small set of requests after a canary deploy. We're rolling back and monitoring; no wide customer impact expected." shall I publish?

oncall-mira: hold on publishing. wait until we confirm SLOs back to normal for 10m. update me in 5.

sam-eng: rollback complete. all canary pods running previous image. 0/2 canary hosts remain in canary pool.

oncall-mira: metrics: error-rate now 0.4% (baseline). p95 within normal. holding for 10m before close.

charlie-sre: captured artifacts: core dump uploaded to /artifacts/incident-2968412370/, stack trace pinned to ticket #INC-6271. root cause hypothesis: regress in fused-attn kernel under seq-length heavy workloads. assigning to eng-research.

pm-liz: thanks team. I'll coordinate postmortem with eng-research and schedule a decision on whether to revert kernel change in mainline.

support-jordan: publishing customer note now (soft banner): "We briefly rolled back a canary release after elevated errors were observed. We don't expect production impact; we're investigating."

oncall-mira: ack the page close in PD once we've held 10m clean. I'll hand off to next oncall for monitoring.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by oncall-mira. Incident status: mitigated, monitoring.

oncall-mira: handing off to @charlie-sre for overnight watch and follow-up. charlie, please own the postmortem and ensure alerts are tuned to reduce noise.

charlie-sre: will do. creating postmortem draft and follow-up task list.

oncall-mira: closing thread here; final note: avoid auto-ramps beyond 10% until kernel PR has a stress test. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed (mitigated).
